strongest_angle: Examine how the United Nations General Assembly voted 164 to 1 on September 4, 2026, to promote map projections that replace the 16th-century Mercator projection and accurately reflect the true size of continents like Africa.

key_facts.fact: By 164 votes to one, Member States at the United Nations General Assembly endorsed a resolution on September 4, 2026, promoting map projections that accurately reflect the true size of continents over the 16th-century Mercator projection.
The United States cast the sole vote against the United Nations resolution, dismissing the initiative as part of a radical ideological project.
The Mercator projection was originally developed in 1569 primarily for ship navigation, which resulted in significant size distortions near the poles.
Representing a spherical globe on a flat two-dimensional surface is a geometric challenge that humanity has attempted to solve for more than 2,000 years.
